questionText:
Given below are two statements:
Statement I: India and Bhutan share open borders and citizens do not require passports to travel between the two nations.
Statement II: Bhutan flushed out anti-India Northeast insurgent groups (ULFA and NDFB) from its territory during Operation All Clear in 2003.

options.text: Both Statement I and Statement II are correct

detailedSolution:
Detailed Solution:
Both Statement I and Statement II are correct. Under the 1949/2007 Friendship Treaty, travel is passport-free, and in December 2003, Bhutan's Royal Army launched Operation All Clear to destroy Indian insurgent camps.
Hence Option A is correct.
Hence, option (C) is correct.

questionText:
Match List-I with List-II

List-I (Convention/Treaty)
(A) Kyoto Protocol
(B) Chemical Weapons Convention
(C) Anti-ballistic Missile (ABM) Treaty
(D) Nuclear Non-Proliferation Treaty

List-II (Year)
(I) 1968
(II) 1972
(III) 1992
(IV) 1997

Choose the correct answer from the options given below:

options.mistakeAnalysis: Correct answer. Correctly maps each entity across columns.
Incorrect option. Inverts the governing property or boundary condition.
Incorrect option. Applies an adjacent or reciprocal mathematical relation.
Incorrect option. Confuses related NCERT concepts or attributes.

detailedSolution:
Detailed Solution:
Detailed Solution:
NCERT Class 12 Contemporary World Politics: (A) Kyoto Protocol was agreed upon in 1997 (Match IV). (B) Chemical Weapons Convention (CWC) was concluded in 1992 (Match III). (C) Anti-Ballistic Missile (ABM) Treaty was signed between the US and USSR in 1972 (Match II). (D) Nuclear Non-Proliferation Treaty (NPT) was opened for signature in 1968 (Match I). Matching: (A)-(IV), (B)-(III), (C)-(II), (D)-(I).
Hence, option (D) is the correct match.
Hence, option (A) is the correct match.
